concepts.title: Need for Reconciliation of Cash Book and Pass Book
concepts.definition: The balance of the bank column of the cash book rarely agrees with the pass book balance because the bank records transactions at its own time, so a reconciliation is prepared to explain and verify the difference.
concepts.key_idea: Reconciliation detects timing differences and errors, and confirms the accuracy of both the cash book and the pass book.

Check that the statement explains the full difference and arrives at the adjusted balance.

concepts.title: Timing Differences and Errors
concepts.definition: Timing differences arise when transactions are recorded in one book earlier than the other, as with cheques issued but not yet presented, cheques deposited but not yet credited, and bank charges, interest or direct debits known to the bank only.
concepts.key_idea: Cheques issued reduce the cash book at once but the pass book later, while deposits in transit do the reverse, so the two balances drift apart until the bank acts.

concepts.title: Bank Reconciliation Statement from Cash Book Balance
concepts.definition: Starting with the debit balance of the cash book, add cheques issued but not presented and credits recorded by the bank directly, and deduct cheques deposited but not credited and bank charges, to arrive at the pass book balance.
concepts.key_idea: Each adjustment reverses the timing difference so that the adjusted figure equals the balance shown by the bank.

solution_steps.explain: Add cheques issued but not yet presented to the cash book balance
Deduct cheques deposited but not yet credited to arrive at the pass book balance

concepts.title: Reconciliation Starting from an Overdraft
concepts.definition: When the cash book shows a credit bank balance, the firm enjoys an overdraft, and the reconciliation statement starts with the minus overdraft and applies the opposite adjustments to arrive at the overdraft as per the pass book.
concepts.key_idea: An overdraft is a liability of the firm to the bank, so its treatment in the statement is the reverse of a favourable balance.

solution_steps.explain: Start the statement with the minus overdraft as per the cash book.
Apply adjustments opposite to the favourable balance case.
Confirm the closing figure equals the overdraft as per the pass book.

concepts.title: Adjusted Cash Book Balance after Bank Items
concepts.definition: Items known only from the pass book, such as bank charges, interest credited or direct collections by the bank, first adjust the cash book, and the remaining timing differences then explain the rest of the difference.
concepts.key_idea: The corrected cash book balance after bank items is the true bank balance, and the leftover unpresented and uncredited cheques complete the reconciliation.
